page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM hypervisor virtualization, it features 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via Hyper-Threading, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU, and operates with dedicated CPU allocation. It includes no integrated GPU hardware and lacks local disk storage, relying on network attached storage alongside a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reflect mid-range performance for multi-threaded processing contrasted with lower single-core speeds. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core (score 945.0), fall into the bottom 25th percentile. In contrast, multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core (23515.32) and Geekbench multi-core (8272.0), achieve average category rankings within the middle 50th percentile. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 98.48 GB/sec for read operations and 49.01 GB/sec for write operations.

In application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates consistent throughput across network and database services, recording 22.12 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 13.89 GB/sec in static web serving. Software compilation using Clang recorded an average score of 18320.0. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides adequate balance for multi-threaded general workloads, container orchestration, web application serving, and compilation pipelines where lower single-core execution speed is acceptable.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a dedicated general-purpose cloud instance built on x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 16 physical cores, 32 vCPUs, and 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation. The instance features no local disk storage or onboard GPU accelerators, relying on network storage and providing 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate weak single-core performance alongside average multi-core processing capability, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 23181.17 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8272.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 98.48 GB/sec for uncached reads. Application testing highlights steady throughput for multi-threaded workloads, achieving 22.12 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.89 GB/sec in static web serving. It is well suited for general-purpose workloads, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier network services.
